 De’Andre Hunter (hip) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Lakers. 
 Hunter returned to the starting lineup Wednesday after a one-game absence due to a hip injury. He’s on the injury report for Friday as questionable with the same hip injury. Dylan Cardwell could move into the starting lineup if Hunter is out again.

 #15 
 De’Andre Hunter scored 24 points (7-of-13 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, two steals, and two 3-pointers in 41 minutes in loss to Blazers. 
 The Kings needed the offense in this one with Darius Acuff having a down game, and Hunter gave them some solid offense. He got the line a lot in this game which is a rarity. This isn’t a sign to add De’Andre Hunter, but it’s more of a reminder that he can be useful as a points streamer if your schedule permits it.

 Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, De’Andre Hunter, Precious Achiuwa and Dylan Cardwell will start Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 The Kings are without Domantas Sabonis (knee) for Sunday’s game, opening up a spot in the starting lineup. Cardwell will replace him, and the Kings will need his rebounding and defense. Also, Hunter reclaims his place in the lineup with Leaky Black heading to the bench. And Achiuwa remains in the starting lineup despite Keegan Murray returning from an ankle injury.

 The Sacramento Kings will start Darius Acuff, Zach LaVine, Leaky Black, Precious Achiuwa, and Domantas Sabonis on Friday. 
 DeAndre Hunter (illness) will not play against the Spurs on Friday, so Leaky Black will get the start. Leaky has been an energy guy who has gained some favor in the eyes of Doug Christie. If you’re in a deeper league, Leaky Black could be worth a stream, but the ball won’t be in his hands with this current iteration of the Kings.

 Scottie Barnes led the Raptors with 29 points (14-of-21 FGs), five rebounds, five assists and one steal in a 105-102 win over the Pistons on Friday.
 Barnes returned from a one-game absence, which was the second leg of a back-to-back just a few days after a four-game absence with a groin injury, and his presence was immediately felt as Toronto snapped a six-game losing streak. He hit a game-winning layup to put them up 103-102 before they got a stop on the other end to seal the win. Barnes is averaging 26.3 points per game over his last three appearances as he tries to keep the Raptors afloat despite all their recent injuries. He’ll look to keep that going against the Bucks on Monday.

 Allen Graves started on Friday and contributed 20 points (6-of-9 FGs), 10 rebounds, one assist, three steals, one block and two three-pointers against the Pistons.
 Graves’ first start couldn’t have gone much better. The rookie recorded the first double-double of his career while also setting career highs for points, rebounds and steals. He got the nod in this game and could remain in that role moving forward with RJ Barrett (hamstring) and Kawhi Leonard (knee) both set to miss more time. Graves is certainly an intriguing piece for dynasty managers, but he could have some redraft value if he continues to start.

 Zion Williamson piled up a team-high 22 points (9-of-19 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists and two steals over 37 minutes in Friday’s loss to the Thunder.
 Williamson went off in the first half, connecting on 7-of-10 from the floor, to help New Orleans open up an eight-point advantage at the break by pouring in a team-high 18 points. He was held to just four points after the break as the Thunder clamped down on him defensively and he converted just 2-of-9 second-half shot attempts. Still, he managed to break 20 points for the eighth time in his last 10 games since the start of November. He’s averaging 21.7 points, 5.4 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.8 steals and 0.6 blocks through 16 games this season. The Pelicans close out a back-to-back with a road matchup against the Spurs on Saturday.
 -  George Bissell

 Aday Mara tallied a season-high 22 points (11-of-15 FGs), 16 rebounds, two assists and two blocks over 29 minutes in Friday’s comeback win over the Pelicans.
 Mara put together a monster all-around fantasy effort, recording career-high marks in both points and rebounds, while also chipping in three blocks. He’s started four of the last five games and six of their last eight overall as Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault has pivoted back to the two-big lineup featuring the 7-foot-3 rookie along with veteran Isaiah Hartenstein while Chet Holmgren remains out with knee tendinitis. The 21-year-old big-man has emerged as a viable fantasy option and should be rostered everywhere until further notice.

 Franz Wagner 
 ORL

 Franz Wagner accumulated 35 points (13-of-25 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, seven assists and one block over 36 minutes to propel the Magic to a 113-111 win over the Nets on Friday.
 Wagner delivered the game-winning bucket on a smooth midrange fadeaway with 2.4 seconds remaining, capping another outstanding performance. He’s continued to thrive with Paolo Banchero sidelined by a high ankle sprain, scoring at least 20 points in seven consecutive games dating back to November 7. He’s topped 30 points five times during that span, rapidly establishing himself as one of fantasy’s most exciting bounce-back performers after injuries limited him to just 34 appearances last season. The Magic have also regained their footing, winning five of their last six games after a brutal 2-9 start. They’ll close out the week with a road matchup against the Wizards on Sunday.
 -  George Bissell 
 Recap

 Julius Randle 
 BKN 
 Forward-Center 
 #30 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Julius Randle amassed a team-high 27 points (9-of-20 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), nine rebounds, six assists and three steals over 39 minutes in Friday’s loss to the Magic.
 Randle didn’t mince words after Brooklyn was embarrassed by Chicago earlier this week, surrendering 21 three-pointers in the lopsided defeat. He backed up his criticism with his play in this one, finishing one rebound shy of his second double-double of the season while narrowly missing out on his third 30-point performance. He was just 1-of-7 from three-point range, but was pretty efficient otherwise. He’s shaken off a frosty start to the year to deliver early-round fantasy value over the last week, averaging nearly 25 points along with five rebounds, four assists and two steals over his last four games. The Nets have a busy four-game week on tap that includes road matchups against the Timberwolves, Bucks, Raptors and Hornets.
 -  George Bissell
